newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT-Yamaichi picks UK soccer winners.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Yamaichi picks UK soccer winners.

text.p: Broker Yamaichi selected English champions Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur Plc and Sunderland Plc as "buys" in a detailed report on Britain's 15 quoted soccer clubs.
The report, by analyst Nigel Hawkins, made "sell" recommendations on Caspian Plc, owners of premier league Leeds United, and Southampton Leisure.
It rated first division promotion candidates Sheffield United a "speculative buy", while including Birmingham City, West Bromwich Albion and Preston North End among its "sell" stocks.
The report noted that the soccer sector had outperformed the market by 40 percent over the last nine months, despite heavy falls in recent weeks.

But it said that stock selection was very important as few clubs could expect to prosper outside the 20-team English premier league. It added that only the premier league's very top clubs stood to benefit greatly from the likely introduction of pay-per-view.
Manchester United, leading the premier league and in the European Cup semifinals, was cited as an obvious takeover target, given the power of its brand.

It rated Sunderland as a "buy" on the basis that it expected the club to avoid relegation from the premier league but it noted that crowds should hold up even if the north-east club were relegated. Southampton was rated a "sell" as it could very well lose its premier league status and as non-football business was not likely to make much of a contribution to operating profit for some time.
The report said the same about Caspian's non-football operations and questioned the attractiveness of the club to pay-per-view audiences beyond its Yorkshire base.
